A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same B-cos LM research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–P support reliable comparison, with no unresolved material gaps.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification and explanation evaluations, a five-annotator human study, ablations, and decoder-only model experiments in Sections 4–7 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original automatic and human evaluations, ablations, and decoder-only experiments, including detailed appendix results.

M1.justification: The B-cos architecture, bias and activation removal, alignment computation, joint conversion/fine-tuning, and explanation extraction remain unchanged. The decoder-specific adaptations in Section 7 also match.

E1.justification: Both versions use AG News, IMDB, HateXplain, Wikipedia and OpenWebText training data, and the same nine BLiMP subsets plus IOI. Appendix D reformats BLiMP subset names without changing dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding classification, training-setup, and generation comparisons retain the same comparator membership, including Saloss, RGFS-SA, and Logit/ALTI Logit where previously reported. The newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Sections 4–7 and Appendices D/J retain the same model configurations, training budgets, splits, sample sizes, metrics, and human-study procedures. B values removed from repetitive captions remain specified in Section 4.1.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 3, alignment-pressure and bias analyses in Section 6, and qualitative examples and supplementary analyses in Appendices K–O are retained. Relocated displays do not introduce or remove analyses.

E5.justification: Three-run averaging and the human-study paired t-tests with Bonferroni correction, using alpha = 0.0083, are unchanged. Neither run-count disclosures nor uncertainty-reporting procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All corresponding table data and all 16 figures retain their results. For example, Table 2's B-cos BERT IMDB Comp remains 74.18, and Table 6's B-cos GPT-2 BLiMP MRR remains 0.7561. Qualitative findings also match.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and the dynamic linear representations of transformer components in Appendix C are unchanged. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, or derivations are substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient PLM conversion, improved explanation faithfulness and human interpretability, competitive task performance, and exploratory extension to decoder-only models.

C2.justification: Interpretations of alignment pressure, sparsity, reduced capacity, and amplified bias remain unchanged. Section 10 shortens existing discussion while retaining the limitations concerning token interactions and tasks requiring multi-step reasoning or external knowledge.

D1.justification: v4's abstract newly provides a code-availability statement and repository pointer, absent from v3. Appendix D's hyperparameters, hardware, training times, baseline implementations, and data-processing instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds six cited works: Abbasi et al. (2025), Ye et al. (2025), Balkir et al. (2022), Wang and Demberg (2024a, 2024b), and Wang et al. (2025b). These extend attribution and bias/fairness context without substantially revising the work's research positioning.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized wording corrections and trims repetitive prose, including the human-evaluation description and limitations. It adds the publication header and OpenReview line while retaining the main section and appendix organization.

P2.justification: All 16 figures and 15 tables remain, with limited resizing, relocation, and caption shortening. Table 6 moves alongside the generation experiments, and Tables 14–15 clarify existing B-cos column labels with GPT-2 and Llama-3.2 model names.

improvement.justification: v4 adds a previously missing code repository pointer, improves result navigation by placing Table 6 with Section 7, and clarifies appendix table labels. Updated references and modest editing provide additional limited benefits. The method, empirical evidence, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
